review.reason: The project is a library and a command-line program. It has no web interface for a browser-driving review to exercise.

always: the five gates: both pytest markers, ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy --strict
test-driven development, with the failing case stated in the verdict
the register invariant: the key count of tests/foxio_deviations.json equals the xfailed count
heavyProofOnlyWhen: a change can move a fingerprint
a change alters a published output field or the output schema
a FoxIO reading or a divergence register entry is at stake
heavyProofMeans: mutation reversal proofs, with the mutation proven live and discriminating in both directions
byte-identical replay of every committed capture
verificationDepth.note: Epics 7, 8 and 9 are database enrichment, documentation and packaging. No fingerprint moves in them, so the heavy proof is not mandatory. The project manager applies it where conformance is actually at stake, and a worker may always apply more than the floor.

docsMcp.note: No documentation MCP server is connected and no concrete marketplace source exists in this repository. Workers read vendor documentation with WebFetch, which .claude/rules/external-apis.md requires.

notes: .github/workflows/test.yml triggers on push and on pull_request for branches [master, dev]. A batch pull request into dev usually starts a run, and #459 measured two that started none. Never read an absent run as a passed run: gh pr checks writes "no checks reported" and that line refuses no merge. Read .claude/rules/batch-gate.md and run `python -m tests.batch_gate --pr <number>` before every batch merge. It exits non-zero on an absent run, on a run that has not finished, and on a run that concluded anything other than success.

A skip keyword anywhere in a commit message creates no run for that commit, subject or body, and GitHub reads no intent. That is the cause #459 measured on pull request #444 and pull request #458: each head commit message held the sentence that states the commit carries no [skip ci]. An assignment commit on an integration branch therefore names the keyword nowhere. .claude/rules/batch-gate.md states the three rules.
publish.yml triggers on a published release only, so a merge to dev deploys nothing. Stage D is skipped.

Worktree policy from session 6. The harness owns every worktree. The project manager launches a worker with isolation "worktree" and never calls EnterWorktree. A worker never calls EnterWorktree or ExitWorktree either, because that pin is session-scoped and every live agent shares it. The project manager stays in the repository root and names an absolute path on every git command.

The system Python holds no scapy and no cryptography. A worker builds a virtual environment before it runs any gate. .venv/ and venv/ are ignored from session 6, so the environment may live in the worktree.

Verification is tiered from 2026-08-08. The floor binds every issue; the heavy proof binds only conformance-affecting work. The heavy discipline found a real defect on nearly every issue of Epics 4 to 6, including two tautological assertions inside tests a worker had just written, so it is dialled back rather than dropped.

A member's pull request carries [skip ci], so its cases may never have run on Linux until the batch gate. #279 sub-merged with macOS-only proof and failed four ubuntu-latest jobs at the gate of batch #361. Expect a platform-only failure there, and confirm dev is green after a merge rather than trusting the pull request run alone.

linuxHost.note: The development laptop is macOS, so a Linux-only failure was unreproducible before this host. It is shared: it runs an Elasticsearch node and continuous integration runners. Read `uptime` before a heavy run and never run a load generator on it.
linuxHost.caveat: It does not reproduce every ubuntu-latest failure. The memory ceiling controls of #279 failed on ubuntu-latest and passed here, because the failure needs an import transient that a constrained runner has and a 137 GiB host does not. Use it to verify a Linux code path, not to predict a Linux continuous integration result.

filingRule.rule: No issue is filed whose only symptom is a stale citation, or a record that describes a past state.
howAWorkerApplies: Repair what your own change falsifies, in the same pull request, even where another live batch owns the file. The project manager resolves the conflict once at sub-merge.
A finding that does not fit the change becomes a comment on an issue that exists, and never a new issue.
A finding that is a defect of the library, or that moves a fingerprint, is still filed. This rule reaches a record and it reaches no measurement of the product.
filingRule.why: A read of 2026-08-15 measured the last 300 commits of master. 56 touch a file under ja4plus/, 192 touch docs/specs/spec.md and 186 touch CHANGELOG.md, against 333 closed issues. The bookkeeping had become the deliverable. A guard that tightens finds more of what it now refuses, so the backlog regenerated itself. #708 and #714 exist only because a batch-ownership rule forbade a worker from repairing a file it had just falsified.
